2026-11-28.headline: Can a printed ear keep its shape?
2026-11-28.summary: Researchers printed an ear-shaped scaffold from alginate and nanocellulose. It held its contours, while the early cell tests left long-term viability an open question.

2026-11-28.headline: Spotting three stages of blood vessel growth on a chip
2026-11-28.summary: An image classifier identified three stages of vessel development on a chip. The team used those stages to time gene-expression measurements.

2026-11-29.headline: Watching skin cells build an epidermis on a chip
2026-11-29.summary: Live imaging on StrataChip captured human skin cells dividing and moving as layers formed. Researchers paired those observations with single-cell gene measurements.

figure.alt: Day-seven microscopy cross-section of the layered epidermis in StrataChip

2026-11-29.headline: A silk bioink gives bone-forming cells a firmer foothold
2026-11-29.summary: A silk-and-albumin formulation held its printed shape and helped rabbit marrow cells attach in laboratory tests. The authors also measured early markers of bone formation.

2026-11-30.headline: A lab-grown arteriole that can change its diameter
2026-11-30.summary: A human vessel model roughly 200 micrometres wide matured under flow and changed its diameter in response to biochemical and metabolic cues.

2026-11-30.headline: How hydrogels could keep cell signals at a bone injury
2026-11-30.summary: A review examines hydrogels that hold and release signalling vesicles near a bone defect. It identifies dose consistency and long-term safety as open questions.
